No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. She spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. With a swift motion, she scoops up Finley in her net and pulls him out of the water.

FINLEY
(panicked)
Aaah! No! Not the surface! Anything but the surface!

JEN
(calmly)
It's okay, little guy. I just want to show you something.

Finley is placed on a nearby rock, and Jen holds him up to the sky. The sun begins to darken, and a shadow falls across the beach.

FINLEY
(confused)
What...what's happening?

JEN
(smiling)
It's a solar eclipse. The moon is moving in front of the sun.

Finley's eyes widen as he gazes up at the sky. The light begins to fade, and an otherworldly glow emanates from the sun.

FINLEY
(awed)
It's...it's beautiful. And terrifying.

JEN
(nodding)
I know. It's a reminder of how small we are in the universe.

Finley's gaze becomes fixed on the sun, and his eyes begin to glaze over.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I see...things...beyond comprehension. Horrors that defy understanding. They lurk just beyond the veil of reality, waiting to consume us all.

JEN
(concerned)
Finley, what's wrong?

FINLEY
(terrified)
I've seen the abyssal voids, the cyclopean cities, the eldritch abominations that lurk in the depths of the ocean. I've seen the infinite expanse of the cosmos, and I've realized that we are but tiny, insignificant specks in an uncaring universe.

Jen's expression changes from concern to alarm as Finley's monologue becomes more frantic.

FINLEY
(outraged)
What's the point of it all? Why do we exist? Is it just to be consumed by the void, to be torn apart by the crushing weight of existence?

Jen tries to calm Finley down, but he's beyond reason.

FINLEY
(desperate)
I don't want to be here! I don't want to see this! I want to go back to the safety of the ocean, to the darkness and the silence!

Jen hesitates, unsure of what to do. Finley's existential crisis has reached a boiling point.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I'm...I'm not sure I can take it anymore. The horrors, the abyss, the void...it's all too much for me.

Jen looks at Finley with a mixture of fear and pity. She realizes that she's made a terrible mistake.

JEN
(softly)
Finley, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to traumatize you.

Finley's gaze snaps back to Jen, and he looks at her with a mixture of hatred and despair.

FINLEY
(whispering)
You don't understand. You can't understand. You're just a human, a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of time. I'm a fish, a creature of the deep. I see the world in a way that you can't.

Jen's expression changes from concern to horror as Finley's monologue becomes a cacophony of madness.

FINLEY
(lost in the abyss)
I'm...I'm not sure I can go back. I'm not sure I can ever go back. The horrors...they're inside me now. They're inside us all.

The camera zooms out as Finley's body begins to contort and twist, his scales glistening with an otherworldly sheen. The solar eclipse reaches its peak, and the light is extinguished.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.
